fieldMarks: 17.3-20.9 in; rounder head and shorter bill than Canvasback, with a pale band near the bill tip.
Male: rufous head and gray (not white) back.
Female: plain brown, plainer-faced than female Ring-necked Duck and without its peaked head.
Call like a cat's meow; also quacks.
behavior: Females often lay eggs in other ducks' nests, and some may be entirely parasitic.
Winter flocks on coastal lagoons can run to tens of thousands.
Dives in water a few feet deep or dabbles; eats mainly aquatic plants (shoalgrass, pondweeds), plus insects in summer.
Migrates in flocks, fairly late in fall and early in spring; males fly north to molt after leaving mates.
habitat: Nests in large marshes in the prairies or intermountain valleys.
Winters mainly on coastal bays and lagoons and on inland freshwater lakes.
range: Breeds mainly in western North America's prairies and intermountain valleys and winters across the southern United States, with big concentrations on Gulf coast lagoons such as the Laguna Madre; recorded across all Canadian and U.S. regions.

lookalikes.name: Canvasback
